literal: Without withholding, gladly giving, eye-like people, even from, not begging, ten million, will yield.
translation: Even from those who are as dear as one's own eyes, who give gladly without hiding anything, refraining from begging is ten million times better.
modern: தம்மிடம் உள்ளதை மறைக்காமல், மகிழ்ச்சியோடு கொடுக்கும் கண் போன்றவரிடத்திலும் கூட, இரந்து கேட்காமல் இருப்பது கோடி மடங்கு நன்மையைத் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of self-respect and the dread of begging. The poet describes a class of exceptionally generous people who are like one's own eyes, highly cherished and dependable, and who give with joy without concealing what they have. Even from such loving and open-handed individuals, the act of not begging is declared to be worth ten million times more than any gift one might receive. The word 'kōṭi' (ten million) is used here to emphasize that maintaining one's dignity by not begging far outweighs any material gain, even when the giver is extremely close and willing.
